description:
`world.function_type_struct_refs(function)` (world.rs:899) returns ONE vec per
function covering `@spec` params/result/constraints, the extern contract, and
every clause's param annotations. It is written from a single walk at
source_publish.rs:404-412, which appends all three families into one
`struct_refs`.

THREE jobs iterate the whole vec and take a `StructDefined` wait on every entry:

    jobs/contract.rs:63   derive_function_contract
    jobs/dispatch.rs:132  plan_entry_dispatch
    jobs/body.rs:267      LowerFunction

So `plan_entry_dispatch` waits on a struct referenced only by an `@spec` return
type, `derive_function_contract` waits on one referenced only by a param
annotation, and `LowerFunction` waits on both. `body.rs:267`'s own comment
describes it as waiting on "the extern spec's struct refs", though the vec also
carries `@spec` and param-annotation refs.

## This is a REFINEMENT, not a correctness bug -- and that is verified

The shared vec is a SUPERSET of what each consumer's own positions need, so there
is no under-wait and no silent-drop path. `dedup_module_ids` (world.rs:892-894)
already collapses repeats. Waiting on an extra `StructDefined` that settles adds
a harmless read edge; waiting on a non-struct surfaces the not-a-struct error
regardless of which job reports it.

## Fix

Split the recorded refs per-consumer -- spec, guard/param-annotation, extern --
so each job waits only on the structs its own positions reference. The single
walk in source_publish.rs already visits the three families separately (three
distinct loops at lines 405-411), so the split is at the RECORDING end, not a new
traversal.

## What the old ticket got wrong

It names TWO consumers. A third (body.rs:267) was added afterwards and
over-waits the same way, so the split must cover all three call sites.

## Checks

- After the split, a function whose `@spec` names `%A{}` and whose param
  annotation names `%B{}` has `plan_entry_dispatch` waiting on
  `StructDefined(B)` only, and `derive_function_contract` on `StructDefined(A)`
  only.
- Telemetry-observed: the per-job wait set shrinks on a fixture with disjoint
  spec/annotation struct refs; total drive work unchanged or lower.
- Coordinate with fz-b6w and the fz-rh2.17.5.6.10 obligation model, which share
  this walk.
title: function_type_struct_refs is one shared wait-set read by three consumers, each over-waiting on the others' struct references
